title: DevProof proof report
description: The complete result of verifying one subject. It records what was checked, not merely whether it passed, so a consumer can tell a verification that proved a great deal from one that proved very little. Unlike the input documents, this schema describes output: DevProof produces it and nothing decodes it strictly, so a consumer that ignores an unrecognized field degrades safely. What must not change is the meaning of a field that is present. Messages are not a stable API; codes and field meanings are.

integrity.description: Whether the artifact's own parts agree. Always evaluated; there is no flag that disables it.

trust.description: Whether evidence satisfied the supplied policy. Without a policy this is not-evaluated, which is never a pass.

semantics.description: Whether a caller-supplied validator accepted the payload. DevProof has no opinion about payload meaning, so this is not-evaluated unless a caller supplied one.

subjectDigest.description: What was verified. A result always names its subject by digest, never by the tag it may have been reached through (DP-007).

treeDigest.description: The payload's identity, independent of its encoding. Recomputed from the layer rather than read from the config.

format.description: The bundle format version that was read.

acceptedIdentities.description: The signers whose signatures verified and whose identities a policy rule accepted. Only signers a rule named appear; listing an unexamined signer beside a trusted one would make the field useless for the question it answers.

acceptedEvidence.description: The evidence the conclusion rests on. Two statements from one trusted signer can say entirely different things about an artifact, so the signer alone does not identify what was verified.

rejectedEvidence.description: Candidates that did not verify, kept separate from findings so "the policy was not satisfied" and "somebody attached junk" stay distinguishable.

policyDigest.description: The policy that was applied, so a result can be re-checked against the rules that produced it.

policyName.description: The policy's metadata name, for diagnostics.

trustRoots.description: The trust material by digest. The same policy reaches different conclusions under different roots. Digests rather than paths: trust material is not a secret, but its location on a machine is not a fact about the result.

evaluatedAt.description: The single time every time-dependent rule used, so two rules in one evaluation cannot disagree about now.

evidenceStorage.description: How evidence was found. The fallback tag scheme cannot express a set and silently replaces, so a consumer needs to know which mode produced the answer (DP-028).

limits.description: The bounds this verification actually ran under and where each came from (DP-021). Every bound appears, including the ones left at their defaults, because a reader cannot tell a default from an omission.

status.description: not-evaluated is never a pass. A dimension nobody checked cannot satisfy a requirement (DP-014).

predicateType.description: What the statement claims to be.

transparencyLogVerified.description: Whether an inclusion proof was checked, not merely whether a log entry was referenced.

integratedTime.description: The authenticated signing time, when one exists. Absent means no trusted time was established, which is not the same as recent.

viaTagFallback.description: Found under the fallback tag scheme rather than the referrers API.

name.description: The bound's stable name, matching the policy field that sets it.

value.description: The effective bound: the smallest anybody asked for (DP-021).

origin.description: Which input supplied that value. A policy that tightened a bound and a client that did are the same number and very different facts about who decided it.

code.description: A stable machine identifier. Codes are an API; messages are not.

rule.description: The policy path the finding came from, such as evidence.maxAge.

subject.description: The affected digest, evidence, source, or path.
